children: SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Digital travel platform Agoda has published its

, spotlighting five key trends and insights poised to shape the next year of travel in Asia and South Korea. Agoda's report points to increased appetite for international travel, alongside the rapid rise of AI in trip planning and growing interest in experiences that reflect travelers' passions, from food and culture to shopping and outdoor pursuits.

Based on research across more than 3,300 travelers from 11 markets in Asia, the 2027 Agoda Asia Travel Pulse also reveals that South Korean travelers are making considered choices about how they spend. Many expect to take fewer but longer trips, while looking for strong value and greater ease across the whole journey.
Alex Park, Country Director, South Korea at Agoda

, said: "South Korean travelers have always been curious about the world, and in 2027 that curiosity is stronger than ever. More than half now plan to travel mostly internationally and they know exactly what they're going for: rich culture and, of course, great food. It's also exciting to see that they're among Asia's most AI-savvy travelers. Agoda will continue to make it easier for South Korean travelers to plan and book trips that are personal, seamless, and great value."
Agoda's top five trends defining travel in South Korea in 2027:
International travel interest remains a priority, despite cost considerations

Following a year of strong interest in overseas travel, South Koreans are looking to travel abroad even more next year. More than a half (51%) of respondents expect to travel mostly outside their own country in 2027—compared with 39% last year—making international travel the leading plan. South Korea ranked third among the 11 markets surveyed for international travel appetite, 13 percentage points above the regional average of 38%. Cost remains a key consideration: more than a third (36%) of respondents say lower travel costs would most help them travel more.
AI becomes a trusted travel planner, with travelers in control

South Korean travelers are increasingly turning to AI to plan their trips, with 60% now using it for travel planning, up from 36% last year. This places South Korea third among AI adoption for the 11 markets surveyed. Still, travelers want to stay in control of their bookings: 39% would only allow an AI agent to book a hotel on their behalf if they could review the booking before confirming, while 34% prefer to book hotels themselves. In 2027, trust will shape the way forward for AI: South Korean travelers say real reviews, clear sources of information and explanations behind recommendations would increase their confidence.
Cuisine and culture top the travel menu

Culinary experiences are the leading motivation for South Koreans planning to travel in 2027, followed by cultural exploration and shopping. Notably, South Korea stands out for its interest in cultural experiences, with 69% of respondents citing cultural exploration as a travel motivation, 15 percentage points above the regional average.Personal interests and hobbies are also a key driver of travel choices, with 69% of respondents saying these influence their decisions. Meanwhile, social media and environmental considerations are gaining prominence, cited by 31% and 34% of South Korean respondents, respectively, up from 13% and 4% last year.
Making each trip count: interest in fewer trips, longer stays

South Korean travelers are trading trip frequency for value. The most common plan for next year is to take one to three trips (53%), up from 30% last year. At the same time, the number of travelers expecting their trips to last thirteen days or longer has tripled compared with last year. For many, the goal is no longer to travel more often, but to travel better, go further, and stay longer.
Destination comes first, while location matters most in accommodation choices

Four in five South Korean travelers (80%) say choosing a destination is their first step when planning a leisure trip, the highest share among the 11 markets surveyed and 16 percentage points above the regional average. Accommodation comes next, with location emerging as the top consideration for 39% of respondents, followed by reviews and ratings (25%). Only 18% cite price as their top consideration when choosing accommodation, the lowest share in Asia and 14 percentage points below the regional average of 32%, indicating that South Koreans are more likely to seek out convenience and comfort over value.
